chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: A believer's emancipation is not [complete/perfect] except through four [qualities].

The first of them is that he be truthful in his narration; the second is that he fulfills what has been imposed upon him of obligatory duties; the third is that he fulfills what has been imposed upon him of supererogatory [duties]; and the fourth is that he be patient with the trials of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What are the four qualities that perfect a believer's faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to define the comprehensive state of *kamal* (perfection), distinguishing between the foundational pillars of faith and the voluntary acts that elevate spiritual rank. This framework reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of orthopraxy (fulfilling obligations) and orthopraxy of the heart (patience and truthfulness) as the markers of a mature believer. The inclusion of supererogatory acts highlights the concept of *ziyadah* (incremental growth) in piety beyond the minimum requirements of Sharia.
